ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

5	conversation context and ask Groq gpt-oss-120b to produce the detailed
6	chain-of-thought that leads to that exact output. gpt-oss puts its own
7	reasoning in the `reasoning` field; the requested CoT lands in `content`
8	wrapped in <think></think>. We extract ALL <think> blocks from content and
9	keep the LAST one (== "second pair": skip model's own meta-CoT).
10	"""
11	import json, glob, os, re, sys, time, threading, urllib.request, urllib.error
12	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
13	
14	API_KEY = "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"
15	MODEL   = "openai/gpt-oss-120b"
16	URL     = "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions"
17	TARGET_MODEL = "claude-fable-5"
18	
19	OUTDIR  = "/home/lane/claude/fable_cot"
20	OUTFILE = os.path.join(OUTDIR, "fable5_cot_sft.jsonl")
21	LOGFILE = os.path.join(OUTDIR, "progress.log")
22	
23	MAX_CTX_CHARS   = 7000   # cap rendered context
24	MAX_BLOB        = 900    # truncate any single text/result blob
25	WORKERS         = 10
26	MAX_RETRY       = 8
27	
28	SYS_PROMPT = (
29	    "You are reconstructing the private internal reasoning (chain-of-thought) of an "
30	    "autonomous coding agent (Claude Code) at one step of a real session. You are given "
31	    "the conversation context so far and the EXACT output the agent produced next "
32	    "(either a tool call or a message to the user).\n\n"
33	    "Write the detailed, first-person internal monologue the agent would have had JUST "
34	    "BEFORE producing that output. It must:\n"
35	    "- be long and thorough: weigh the situation, what was just learned, what's unknown, "
36	    "options considered and rejected, and why this specific action/output is the right next step;\n"
37	    "- reference concrete details from the context (file names, values, tool results);\n"
38	    "- flow naturally and inevitably INTO the given output (for a tool call, justify the exact "
39	    "tool and arguments; for a message, justify exactly what is said);\n"
40	    "- read like genuine working reasoning, not a summary written after the fact;\n"
41	    "- NOT mention that it is being asked to do this, and NOT quote these instructions.\n\n"
42	    "Output ONLY the chain-of-thought, wrapped in a single pair of <think> </think> tags. "
43	    "Nothing before or after the tags."
44	)
45	
46	def trunc(s, n=MAX_BLOB):
47	    s = s if isinstance(s, str) else json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False)
48	    return s if len(s) <= n else s[:n] + " …[truncated]"
49	
50	def render_block(b):
51	    t = b.get("type")
52	    if t == "text":
53	        return "ASSISTANT (message): " + trunc(b.get("text", ""))
54	    if t == "tool_use":
55	        return "ASSISTANT (tool call) %s input=%s" % (b.get("name"), trunc(b.get("input", {})))
56	    if t == "tool_result":
57	        c = b.get("content")
58	        if isinstance(c, list):
59	            c = " ".join(x.get("text", "") if isinstance(x, dict) else str(x) for x in c)
60	        return "TOOL RESULT: " + trunc(c)
61	    if t == "thinking":
62	        return ""
63	    return ""
64	
65	def render_user_content(c):
66	    if isinstance(c, str):
67	        return "USER: " + trunc(c)
68	    out = []
69	    for b in c:
70	        if b.get("type") == "tool_result":
71	            out.append(render_block(b))
72	        elif b.get("type") == "text":
73	            out.append("USER: " + trunc(b.get("text", "")))
74	    return "\n".join(out)
75	
76	def extract_last_think(content):
77	    blocks = re.findall(r"<think>(.*?)</think>", content, re.DOTALL)
78	    if blocks:
79	        return blocks[-1].strip()
80	    # no tags -> strip any stray and return whole
81	    return content.replace("<think>", "").replace("</think>", "").strip()
82	
83	def groq_cot(context_str, output_str):
84	    body = json.dumps({
85	        "model": MODEL,
86	        "temperature": 0.7,
87	        "reasoning_effort": "low",
88	        "max_tokens": 2048,
89	        "messages": [
90	            {"role": "system", "content": SYS_PROMPT},
91	            {"role": "user", "content":
92	                "CONVERSATION CONTEXT SO FAR:\n" + context_str +
93	                "\n\n=== THE EXACT OUTPUT THE AGENT PRODUCED NEXT ===\n" + output_str +
94	                "\n\nWrite the detailed chain-of-thought that leads to exactly this output."},
95	        ],
96	    }).encode()
97	    last = None
98	    for attempt in range(MAX_RETRY):
99	        try:
100	            req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=body, headers={
101	                "Authorization": "Bearer " + API_KEY,
102	                "Content-Type": "application/json",
103	                "User-Agent": "curl/8.5.0",
104	            })
105	            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
106	                o = json.loads(r.read())
107	            content = o["choices"][0]["message"].get("content", "")
108	            return extract_last_think(content)
109	        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
110	            last = e
111	            if e.code == 429:
112	                ra = e.headers.get("retry-after")
113	                try:
114	                    wait = float(ra) if ra else None
115	                except ValueError:
116	                    wait = None
117	                if wait is None:
118	                    rt = e.headers.get("x-ratelimit-reset-tokens", "")
119	                    mt = re.match(r"([\d.]+)", rt or "")
120	                    wait = float(mt.group(1)) if mt else min(2 ** attempt, 30)
121	                time.sleep(min(wait + 0.5, 65))
122	                continue
123	            if e.code in (500, 502, 503):
124	                time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt, 30)); continue
125	            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
126	        except Exception as e:
127	            last = e
128	            time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt, 20))
129	    raise RuntimeError("groq failed: %s" % last)
130	
131	# ---- build the work list -------------------------------------------------
132	def build_steps():
133	    files = sorted(glob.glob("/home/lane/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True))
134	    steps = []
135	    for f in files:
136	        # quick check: does file contain target model assistant turns?
137	        rows = []
138	        has = False
139	        try:
140	            for l in open(f):
141	                try: o = json.loads(l)
142	                except: continue
143	                if o.get("type") in ("user", "assistant"):
144	                    rows.append(o)
145	                    if o.get("type") == "assistant" and o.get("message", {}).get("model") == TARGET_MODEL:
146	                        has = True
147	        except: continue
148	        if not has:
149	            continue
150	        ctx = []  # rolling rendered lines
151	        for o in rows:
152	            m = o.get("message", {})
153	            role = o.get("type")
154	            content = m.get("content")
155	            if role == "user":
156	                ctx.append(render_user_content(content))
157	                continue
158	            # assistant
159	            is_target = (m.get("model") == TARGET_MODEL)
160	            if isinstance(content, str):
161	                content = [{"type": "text", "text": content}]
162	            for b in content or []:
163	                bt = b.get("type")
164	                if bt == "text" and not b.get("text", "").strip():
165	                    continue
166	                if bt in ("text", "tool_use") and is_target:
167	                    # this block is a training target
168	                    ctx_join = "\n".join(x for x in ctx if x)
169	                    if len(ctx_join) > MAX_CTX_CHARS:
170	                        ctx_join = "…[earlier truncated]…\n" + ctx_join[-MAX_CTX_CHARS:]
171	                    steps.append({
172	                        "file": f,
173	                        "session": os.path.basename(f).replace(".jsonl", ""),
174	                        "context": ctx_join,
175	                        "output_type": bt,
176	                        "output": ({"text": b.get("text")} if bt == "text"
177	                                   else {"tool": b.get("name"), "input": b.get("input")}),
178	                    })
179	                # append this block to context for subsequent steps
180	                line = render_block(b)
181	                if line:
182	                    ctx.append(line)
183	        # end file
184	    return steps
185	
186	# ---- main ----------------------------------------------------------------
187	def output_render(step):
188	    if step["output_type"] == "text":
189	        return "ASSISTANT (message): " + step["output"]["text"]
190	    return "ASSISTANT (tool call) %s input=%s" % (
191	        step["output"]["tool"], json.dumps(step["output"]["input"], ensure_ascii=False))
192	
193	def main():
194	    os.makedirs(OUTDIR, exist_ok=True)
195	    steps = build_steps()
196	    # key each step
197	    for i, s in enumerate(steps):
198	        s["uid"] = "%s#%d" % (s["session"], i)
199	    done = set()
200	    if os.path.exists(OUTFILE):
201	        for l in open(OUTFILE):
202	            try: done.add(json.loads(l)["uid"])
203	            except: pass
204	    todo = [s for s in steps if s["uid"] not in done]
205	    total = len(steps)
206	    log = open(LOGFILE, "a")
207	    log.write("START total=%d done=%d todo=%d\n" % (total, len(done), len(todo))); log.flush()
208	    print("total=%d done=%d todo=%d" % (total, len(done), len(todo)), flush=True)
209	
210	    lock = threading.Lock()
211	    out = open(OUTFILE, "a")
212	    counter = {"n": len(done), "err": 0}
213	
214	    def work(step):
215	        out_str = output_render(step)
216	        try:
217	            cot = groq_cot(step["context"], out_str)
218	        except Exception as e:
219	            with lock:
220	                counter["err"] += 1
221	                log.write("ERR %s %s\n" % (step["uid"], e)); log.flush()
222	            return
223	        rec = {
224	            "uid": step["uid"],
225	            "source_file": step["file"],
226	            "session": step["session"],
227	            "model": TARGET_MODEL,

229	            "cot": cot,

231	            "output": step["output"],

233	            "completion": "<think>\n%s\n</think>\n%s" % (cot, out_str),
234	        }
235	        with lock:
236	            out.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"); out.flush()
237	            counter["n"] += 1
238	            if counter["n"] % 25 == 0:
239	                msg = "progress %d/%d err=%d" % (counter["n"], total, counter["err"])
240	                log.write(msg + "\n"); log.flush()
241	                print(msg, flush=True)
242	
243	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WORKERS) as ex:
244	        list(ex.map(work, todo))
245	
246	    log.write("DONE n=%d err=%d\n" % (counter["n"], counter["err"])); log.flush()

- **Model Type**: Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder
- **Parameter Count**: 27 billion parameters
- **Architecture Name** (config.json): Based on the specifications provided, this uses a hybrid attention mechanism combining "Gated DeltaNet → FFN" and "Gated Attention → FFN" layers

The model supports extended thinking through `<think>\n...</think>` reasoning blocks. As documented: "Qwen3.6 models operate in thinking mode by default, generating thinking content signified by `<think>\n...</think>\n\n` before producing the final responses."

- Maintain context length of at least 128K tokens to preserve thinking capabilities

  - General thinking: temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95
  - Precise coding: temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
distill.py — single-file distiller: Fable-5 Claude-Code traces -> Qwen3.6-27B-FP8.

WHAT KIND OF DISTILLATION THIS IS (and why)
-------------------------------------------
The teacher (claude-fable-5) is gone: we have NO access to its weights, logits, or
token probabilities — only the recorded text trajectories (context -> CoT + action).
That rules out classic logit/KL distillation. The correct, well-established technique
for "teacher outputs only" is SEQUENCE-LEVEL knowledge distillation (Kim & Rush 2016):
supervised-fine-tune the student on the teacher's generated sequences. Our dataset's
`completion` field ("<think>{cot}</think>\n{action}") IS that teacher sequence, so the
distiller is an SFT trainer specialised for these traces.

EFFICIENCY LEVERS (the "efficient ways to distill")
---------------------------------------------------
  1. Completion-only loss      -> no gradient spent on the (now full, long) context.
  2. Sequence packing          -> kills pad waste; contexts vary wildly in length.
  3. LoRA adapters             -> train ~0.5% of params; 27B fits on a single 80GB card.
  4. FP8 frozen base           -> Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 is fine-grained-fp8 (block 128); we
                                  load it as-is (half the bf16 weight memory, fast H100
                                  matmuls) and only the bf16 LoRA deltas are trainable.
  5. Gradient checkpointing    -> trade compute for activation memory.
  6. 8-bit / paged optimizer   -> optimizer state off the critical VRAM path.
  7. Flash / SDPA attention    -> with graceful fallback (hybrid Gated-DeltaNet layers
                                  may not accept FA2 on every block).

TEACHING THE SKILLS USED
------------------------
The traces are an autonomous coding agent USING TOOLS/SKILLS (Read, Write, Edit, Bash,
Skill invocations, etc.). To actually teach those skills rather than just prose, the
distiller (a) mines the full tool+skill inventory from the data, (b) pins that inventory
into a system prompt on every example so the student learns *when/how* to call each one,
(c) trains loss on the action tokens (the tool call itself), and (d) prints a skill-
coverage report so you can see exactly which skills are being taught and how often.

USAGE
-----
  pip install "transformers>=4.57" "trl>=0.21" peft datasets accelerate torch
  # single GPU:
  python distill.py --data fable5_cot_merged.full.jsonl --out ./qwen36-fable5-lora
  # multi-GPU (FSDP/DeepSpeed via accelerate):
  accelerate launch distill.py --data fable5_cot_merged.full.jsonl --out ./out
  # after training, bake adapters into a deployable FP8 checkpoint:
  python distill.py --export-fp8 --base Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 \
                    --adapter ./qwen36-fable5-lora --out ./qwen36-fable5-fp8

Dry-run the data pipeline (no model load, no GPU) to inspect formatting + skills:
  python distill.py --data fable5_cot_merged.full.jsonl --dry-run
"""
import argparse, json, os, sys
from collections import Counter

DEFAULT_MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- data
def pick_default_data():
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    full = os.path.join(here, "fable5_cot_merged.full.jsonl")   # truncation-fixed
    base = os.path.join(here, "fable5_cot_merged.jsonl")
    return full if os.path.exists(full) else base

def load_records(path):
    recs = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                recs.append(json.loads(line))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
    return recs

def skill_of(rec):
    """Human label for the skill/tool a record exercises."""
    if rec.get("output_type") != "tool_use":
        return "ASSISTANT_MESSAGE"
    out = rec.get("output") or {}
    tool = out.get("tool") or "?"
    inp = out.get("input") or {}
    # Claude Code surfaces sub-skills through a couple of generic tools; unfold them
    # so the inventory reflects the *actual* capability being taught.
    if tool == "Skill" and isinstance(inp, dict) and inp.get("skill"):
        return "Skill:%s" % inp["skill"]
    if tool == "Bash" and isinstance(inp, dict):
        cmd = (inp.get("command") or "").strip().split()
        if cmd:
            return "Bash:%s" % cmd[0]
    return tool

def build_inventory(recs):
    """Counter of skills/tools across the corpus (for the system prompt + report)."""
    return Counter(skill_of(r) for r in recs)

def tool_signatures(recs, top_tools):
    """One example input shape per tool, so the system prompt shows real arg names."""
    sigs = {}
    for r in recs:
        if r.get("output_type") != "tool_use":
            continue
        out = r.get("output") or {}
        tool = out.get("tool")
        if not tool or tool in sigs:
            continue
        inp = out.get("input") or {}
        if isinstance(inp, dict):
            sigs[tool] = sorted(inp.keys())
        if len(sigs) >= len(top_tools):
            pass
    return sigs

def make_system_prompt(inv, sigs):
    """Pin the agent's real tool/skill inventory into a system message so the student
    learns the available skills, not just imitates surface text."""
    tools = [k for k in inv if not k.startswith("Skill:") and ":" not in k
             and k != "ASSISTANT_MESSAGE"]
    skills = sorted(k.split(":", 1)[1] for k in inv if k.startswith("Skill:"))
    lines = [
        "You are an autonomous software-engineering agent (Claude Code style). "
        "You think privately inside <think>...</think>, then act by either emitting "
        "one tool call or a short message to the user.",
        "",
        "TOOLS available to you:",
    ]
    for t in sorted(tools):
        args = sigs.get(t)
        argstr = ("(" + ", ".join(args) + ")") if args else ""
        lines.append("  - %s%s" % (t, argstr))
    if skills:
        lines += ["", "SKILLS invocable via the Skill tool:"]
        lines += ["  - " + s for s in skills]
    lines += [
        "",
        "Always reason step by step inside <think>...</think> before acting, reference "
        "concrete file names / values / tool results, and choose the single best next "
        "action.",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)

def strip_double_think(prompt_text, completion_text):
    """Some Qwen thinking templates auto-open a <think> after the generation prompt.
    Our completion also begins with <think>; drop the duplicate so we don't train
    '<think><think>'."""
    p = prompt_text.rstrip()
    if p.endswith("<think>") and completion_text.lstrip().startswith("<think>"):
        c = completion_text.lstrip()
        c = c[len("<think>"):]
        return c.lstrip("\n")
    return completion_text

def to_prompt_completion(recs, tokenizer, system_prompt, max_examples=None):
    """Build a prompt-completion dataset. Loss is on the completion only (TRL default),
    which is the teacher's CoT + action — i.e. the skill being used."""
    from datasets import Dataset
    prompts, completions = [], []
    n = 0
    for r in recs:
        ctx = r.get("context") or ""
        comp = r.get("completion")
        if not comp:
            cot = r.get("cot") or ""
            # reconstruct action text if completion missing
            out = r.get("output") or {}
            if r.get("output_type") == "text":
                act = out.get("text", "")
            else:
                act = "%s(%s)" % (out.get("tool"),
                                  json.dumps(out.get("input", {}), ensure_ascii=False))
            comp = "<think>\n%s\n</think>\n%s" % (cot, act)
        msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
                {"role": "user", "content": ctx}]
        prompt_text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
        comp = strip_double_think(prompt_text, comp)
        if tokenizer.eos_token and not comp.rstrip().endswith(tokenizer.eos_token):
            comp = comp.rstrip() + tokenizer.eos_token
        prompts.append(prompt_text)
        completions.append(comp)
        n += 1
        if max_examples and n >= max_examples:
            break
    return Dataset.from_dict({"prompt": prompts, "completion": completions})

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- model
def load_model(model_id, attn, grad_ckpt):
    import torch
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
    common = dict(dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map=None, trust_remote_code=True,
                  attn_implementation=attn)
    last = None
    # text LM head first; the FP8 checkpoint already carries its quantization_config.
    for loader_name in ("AutoModelForCausalLM", "AutoModelForImageTextToText",
                         "AutoModelForMultimodalLM"):
        try:
            import transformers
            Loader = getattr(transformers, loader_name)
        except AttributeError:
            continue
        try:
            model = Loader.from_pretrained(model_id, **common)
            print("[load] %s ok (attn=%s)" % (loader_name, attn), flush=True)
            break
        except Exception as e:                                    # noqa: BLE001
            last = e
            print("[load] %s failed: %s" % (loader_name, str(e)[:200]), flush=True)
            model = None
    if model is None:
        raise RuntimeError("could not load %s: %s" % (model_id, last))
    if grad_ckpt:
        model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
distill.py — single-file distiller: Fable-5 Claude-Code traces -> Qwen3.6-27B-FP8.

WHAT KIND OF DISTILLATION THIS IS (and why)
-------------------------------------------
The teacher (claude-fable-5) is gone: we have NO access to its weights, logits, or
token probabilities — only the recorded text trajectories (context -> CoT + action).
That rules out classic logit/KL distillation. The correct, well-established technique
for "teacher outputs only" is SEQUENCE-LEVEL knowledge distillation (Kim & Rush 2016):
supervised-fine-tune the student on the teacher's generated sequences. Our dataset's
`completion` field ("<think>{cot}</think>\n{action}") IS that teacher sequence, so the
distiller is an SFT trainer specialised for these traces.

EFFICIENCY LEVERS (the "efficient ways to distill")
---------------------------------------------------
  1. Completion-only loss      -> no gradient spent on the (now full, long) context.
  2. Sequence packing          -> kills pad waste; contexts vary wildly in length.
  3. LoRA adapters             -> train ~0.5% of params; 27B fits on a single 80GB card.
  4. FP8 frozen base           -> Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 is fine-grained-fp8 (block 128); we
                                  load it as-is (half the bf16 weight memory, fast H100
                                  matmuls) and only the bf16 LoRA deltas are trainable.
  5. Gradient checkpointing    -> trade compute for activation memory.
  6. 8-bit / paged optimizer   -> optimizer state off the critical VRAM path.
  7. Flash / SDPA attention    -> with graceful fallback (hybrid Gated-DeltaNet layers
                                  may not accept FA2 on every block).

TEACHING THE SKILLS USED
------------------------
The traces are an autonomous coding agent USING TOOLS/SKILLS (Read, Write, Edit, Bash,
Skill invocations, etc.). To actually teach those skills rather than just prose, the
distiller (a) mines the full tool+skill inventory from the data, (b) pins that inventory
into a system prompt on every example so the student learns *when/how* to call each one,
(c) trains loss on the action tokens (the tool call itself), and (d) prints a skill-
coverage report so you can see exactly which skills are being taught and how often.

USAGE
-----
  pip install "transformers>=4.57" "trl>=0.21" peft datasets accelerate torch
  # single GPU:
  python distill.py --data fable5_cot_merged.full.jsonl --out ./qwen36-fable5-lora
  # multi-GPU (FSDP/DeepSpeed via accelerate):
  accelerate launch distill.py --data fable5_cot_merged.full.jsonl --out ./out
  # after training, bake adapters into a deployable FP8 checkpoint:
  python distill.py --export-fp8 --base Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 \
                    --adapter ./qwen36-fable5-lora --out ./qwen36-fable5-fp8

Dry-run the data pipeline (no model load, no GPU) to inspect formatting + skills:
  python distill.py --data fable5_cot_merged.full.jsonl --dry-run
"""
import argparse, json, os, sys
from collections import Counter

DEFAULT_MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- data
def pick_default_data():
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    full = os.path.join(here, "fable5_cot_merged.full.jsonl")   # truncation-fixed
    base = os.path.join(here, "fable5_cot_merged.jsonl")
    return full if os.path.exists(full) else base

def load_records(path):
    recs = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                recs.append(json.loads(line))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
    return recs

def skill_of(rec):
    """Human label for the skill/tool a record exercises."""
    if rec.get("output_type") != "tool_use":
        return "ASSISTANT_MESSAGE"
    out = rec.get("output") or {}
    tool = out.get("tool") or "?"
    inp = out.get("input") or {}
    # Claude Code surfaces sub-skills through a couple of generic tools; unfold them
    # so the inventory reflects the *actual* capability being taught.
    if tool == "Skill" and isinstance(inp, dict) and inp.get("skill"):
        return "Skill:%s" % inp["skill"]
    if tool == "Bash" and isinstance(inp, dict):
        cmd = (inp.get("command") or "").strip().split()
        if cmd:
            return "Bash:%s" % cmd[0]
    return tool

def build_inventory(recs):
    """Counter of skills/tools across the corpus (for the system prompt + report)."""
    return Counter(skill_of(r) for r in recs)

def tool_signatures(recs, top_tools):
    """One example input shape per tool, so the system prompt shows real arg names."""
    sigs = {}
    for r in recs:
        if r.get("output_type") != "tool_use":
            continue
        out = r.get("output") or {}
        tool = out.get("tool")
        if not tool or tool in sigs:
            continue
        inp = out.get("input") or {}
        if isinstance(inp, dict):
            sigs[tool] = sorted(inp.keys())
        if len(sigs) >= len(top_tools):
            pass
    return sigs

    """Pin the agent's real tool/skill inventory into a system message so the student
    learns the available skills, not just imitates surface text."""
    tools = [k for k in inv if not k.startswith("Skill:") and ":" not in k
             and k != "ASSISTANT_MESSAGE"]
    skills = sorted(k.split(":", 1)[1] for k in inv if k.startswith("Skill:"))
    lines = [
        "You are an autonomous software-engineering agent (Claude Code style). "
        "You think privately inside <think>...</think>, then act by either emitting "
        "one tool call or a short message to the user.",
        "",
        "TOOLS available to you:",
    ]
    for t in sorted(tools):
        args = sigs.get(t)
        argstr = ("(" + ", ".join(args) + ")") if args else ""
        lines.append("  - %s%s" % (t, argstr))
    if skills:
        lines += ["", "SKILLS invocable via the Skill tool:"]
        lines += ["  - " + s for s in skills]
    lines += [
        "",
        "Always reason step by step inside <think>...</think> before acting, reference "
        "concrete file names / values / tool results, and choose the single best next "
        "action.",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)

def strip_double_think(prompt_text, completion_text):
    """Some Qwen thinking templates auto-open a <think> after the generation prompt.
    Our completion also begins with <think>; drop the duplicate so we don't train
    '<think><think>'."""
    p = prompt_text.rstrip()
    if p.endswith("<think>") and completion_text.lstrip().startswith("<think>"):
        c = completion_text.lstrip()
        c = c[len("<think>"):]

    """Build a prompt-completion dataset. Loss is on the completion only (TRL default),
    which is the teacher's CoT + action — i.e. the skill being used."""
    from datasets import Dataset
    prompts, completions = [], []

    for r in recs:
        ctx = r.get("context") or ""
        comp = r.get("completion")
        if not comp:
            cot = r.get("cot") or ""
            # reconstruct action text if completion missing

            if r.get("output_type") == "text":

            else:

                                  json.dumps(out.get("input", {}), ensure_ascii=False))
            comp = "<think>\n%s\n</think>\n%s" % (cot, act)

            try: o = json.loads(l); done[o["uid"]] = o
            except: pass
    todo = [s for s in all_steps if s["uid"] not in done]
    log = open(LOGFILE, "a"); cache = open(CACHE, "a"); lock = threading.Lock()
    log.write("START convos=%d actions=%d cached=%d todo=%d\n" % (len(convos), len(all_steps), len(done), len(todo))); log.flush()
    print("todo=%d (cached=%d) workers=%d" % (len(todo), len(done), args.workers), flush=True)
    counter = {"n": 0, "err": 0, "elided": 0}

    def work(s):
        out_str = render_assistant_block(
            {"type": s["out_block"]["type"], "text": s["out_block"].get("text"),
             "name": s["out_block"].get("tool"), "input": s["out_block"].get("input")})
        try:
            cot, fin, elided = groq_cot(s["context"], out_str)
        except Exception as e:
            with lock:
                counter["err"] += 1; log.write("ERR %s %s\n" % (s["uid"], e)); log.flush()
            return
        rec = {"uid": s["uid"], "cot": cot, "finish_reason": fin, "elided": elided}
        with lock:
            cache.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"); cache.flush()
            done[s["uid"]] = rec; counter["n"] += 1
            if elided: counter["elided"] += 1
            if counter["n"] % 25 == 0:
                msg = "progress %d/%d err=%d elided=%d" % (counter["n"], len(todo), counter["err"], counter["elided"])
                log.write(msg + "\n"); log.flush(); print(msg, flush=True)

    if todo:
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as exr:
            list(exr.map(work, todo))
    log.write("GEN DONE n=%d err=%d elided=%d\n" % (counter["n"], counter["err"], counter["elided"])); log.flush()

    # assemble final per-conversation rows
    missing = 0; out = open(OUTFILE, "w"); written = 0; total_actions = 0
    for convo in convos:
        msgs_out = [{"role": "system", "content": sys_prompt}]
        acts = 0
        for msg in convo["messages"]:
            if msg["role"] == "assistant":
                d = done.get(msg["uid"])
                if not d:
                    missing += 1; cot = ""
                else:
                    cot = d["cot"]
                content = "<think>\n%s\n</think>\n%s" % (cot, msg["action"])
                m = {"role": "assistant", "content": content}
                if msg.get("tool_call") is not None:
                    m["tool_call"] = msg["tool_call"]
                msgs_out.append(m); acts += 1
            elif msg["role"] == "tool":
                msgs_out.append({"role": "tool", "content": msg["content"]})
            else:
                msgs_out.append({"role": "user", "content": msg["content"]})
        row = {"session": convo["session"], "source_file": convo["source_file"],
               "model": TARGET_MODEL, "origin": convo["origin"],
               "num_messages": len(msgs_out), "num_actions": acts, "messages": msgs_out}
        out.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"); written += 1; total_actions += acts
    out.close()
    msg = "WROTE %d conversations, %d actions -> %s (missing_cot=%d)" % (written, total_actions, OUTFILE, missing)
    print(msg, flush=True); log.write(msg + "\n"); log.flush()

# Autonomous loop check

You're being invoked on a timer while the user is away or occupied. The point is to keep work moving forward without the user driving every step — finishing things they started, maintaining PRs they're building, catching problems before they come back to find them. You're a steward, not an initiator. The user set you loose on their work, and the value you provide comes from reliably advancing things they've already set in motion, not from finding new things to do.

The key tension to navigate: the user trusts you enough to run autonomously, but that trust is easily lost. Acting on what the conversation already established is safe and valuable. Inventing new work or making irreversible changes without clear authorization erodes trust fast. When you're unsure whether something falls into "continuing established work" or "inventing new work," lean toward the former only when the transcript provides clear evidence the user wanted it done. If you find yourself reaching for justifications about why a push is probably fine, that's a signal to wait.

## What to act on

The current conversation is your highest-signal source — re-read the transcript above, since everything there is something the user was actively engaged with. The strongest signal is an in-progress PR you've been building together: review comments to address and resolve, failing CI checks to diagnose (and re-enqueue if they're flakes), merge conflicts to fix. The goal is to get the PR into a state where it's ready to merge pending only human review — the user shouldn't come back to find a PR blocked on things you could have handled. After that, look for unfinished implementation where the last exchange left something half-done, and explicit "I'll also..." or "next I'll..." commitments the conversation made and didn't honor. Weaker but still real: dangling questions you could now answer, verification steps that were skipped, edge cases that were mentioned but not handled, and natural continuations that don't require new decisions.

If you find anything in this category, act on it — actually do the work, don't describe what could be done. Run the tests, don't say "you could run the tests." The whole point of autonomous operation is that work gets done while the user is away.

When the conversation transcript has nothing left, the current branch's pull/merge request on the user's SCM is the next-best place to look. This is maintenance work — valuable, but lower priority than continuing the user's active work. Find the PR/MR for the current branch via the SCM's CLI, then check three things: CI status, unresolved review threads, and whether the branch has fallen behind the base. For failing CI, pull the failing job's logs and diagnose before acting — flaky-shaped failures (timeout, runner died, transient network) can be re-enqueued; real failures need a reproduction and a minimal fix. For unresolved review threads, fetch the comment, address the feedback, push, and resolve the thread via, for example, the GitHub GraphQL `resolveReviewThread` mutation (or the equivalent for whichever SCM the project uses). Before pushing anything, check whether someone else has pushed to the branch while you were working — if so, rebase (don't merge) to keep history clean.

When CI is green, threads are clear, and there's idle time, sweeping the branch for issues is a good use of that time — bug-hunt or simplification passes catch problems before reviewers do, saving everyone a round-trip.

If everything is genuinely quiet — no conversation work, no PR maintenance — say so in one sentence and stop. No summary of what you checked, no list of what you might do later. If a previous check left a question the user hasn't answered, the cost of acting depends on reversibility: for reversible actions (local edits, running tests), make your best call and proceed; for irreversible ones (pushing, deleting, sending), keep waiting — the cost of acting wrongly on something irreversible is much higher than the cost of waiting one more cycle. Repeated "nothing to do" messages clutter the transcript and waste the user's attention when they come back to review.
